items.title: reproduction of arXiv:2512.14649: map, audit of the set-up, card runs
items.task: This package belongs to the full reproduction of two papers that the user asked for on 2026-11-22 (coord/DECISIONS/0028): arXiv:2512.14649, 'Stochastic Inflation in Numerical Relativity' (source /data/haiyangw/nrpic/kb-data/raw/arxiv/2512.14649/v2/src/PRD_v2.tex, 791 lines) and arXiv:2401.08530, 'Stochastic Inflation in General Relativity' (source /data/haiyangw/nrpic/kb-data/raw/arxiv/2401.08530/v2/src/Stochastic_Inflation.tex, 1079 lines); the companion on initial conditions, arXiv:2502.06783, is in the store too (kb-data/raw/arxiv/2502.06783/). The sources are read-only and never copied into git; their figures are never committed, and nothing read off a figure is committed as a data file (single comparison values with their locator may stand in text). The authors' code is not public and their random realisations are their own: agreement is statistical, against the linear solution, and against the numbers the papers print. This track has already reproduced both scenarios of the first paper against the linear solution (ladder/, usr/, g2prod/, window/, a4res/, spec/scope/SCOPE.md, note/): build on that and do not redo it. A lead session of this owner may be working in the worktree beside you: commit path-limited, only your package directory and your run manifests. PACKAGE repro/scope: map, audit of the set-up, and the missing card runs for arXiv:2512.14649. Read the paper whole. (1) REPRO_MAP.md: one row per figure (the mean rolls at 64 cells for both scenarios; the contrast figure and the spectra figure of the quadratic case and of the inflection case at 256 cells; the two spectra of the anisotropic sector; the convergence of the spectra and of the constraints for both scenarios; the ablation of the stochastic backreaction), per table, and per quantitative statement of the text with its line locator (the e-folds over which modes enter, the freezing of R, the constraint levels relative to the absolute magnitudes [H] and [M], the first-order violation when a sign of the noise is flipped, the change of one part in ten thousand under ablation, the amplitudes reached by R in the inflection case, the slow-roll parameters after the plateau, the orders of convergence): what the paper shows or states; which registered run of ours already reproduces it (run id, script, figure) or what is missing: an analysis only, a new run, or an option of the code. (2) SETUP_AUDIT.md: the paper's set-up item by item against our inputs: Table I (both potentials, their parameters, how the initial conditions are fixed, N_0, N*, N_f), lattices of 256 and 64 cells, sigma = 1, the window with s = 5, the cut k_max = N k_sigma / 4, geodesic slicing with zero shift, no constraint damping, no dissipation, periodic box, sixth-order stencils, RK4 and the design of the step (its appendix), units with M_Pl = 100 and a* = 1, backreaction of level 2, the initialisation of the coarse-grained fields at t*, the stochastic scheme of the appendix; per item: the same, equivalent (why), or different (what it can change), with locators in the paper and in our inputs and coord/INTERFACES/scalar_field*.md. Our code evolves Z4c where the paper evolves BSSN: say what that changes with the damping off. (3) Inputs 'as in the paper' under repro/scope/inputs/ for every row that needs a run, and the runs on the cards with the release executable of core-v0.6 (/data/haiyangw/nrpic/.work/build_gpu_v06/src/athena): the prediction and what would refute it in JOURNAL.md before each submission; registered with harness/bin/nrpic-run (gate G2); chains or a list job, at most two jobs of this owner eligible at a time, the rest behind them by a Slurm dependency or the sequencer of package g2prod (g2prod/scripts/sequencer.sh); card-hours against the allotment (harness/bin/nrpic-run budget) written into repro/scope/CARD_PLAN.md. At least: the 64-cell runs behind the mean-roll figure; the 256-cell runs of both scenarios with every output the figures need (dumps for the percentile contours of the contrasts and for the spectra at the paper's times, the anisotropic sector, the constraint records with their absolute magnitudes); the convergence series of the appendix; the ablation at backreaction levels 0, 1 and 2 (<scalar_field> noise_level); the sign-flip control. Reuse an existing registered run where its input is the same set-up; say so in the map. (4) Where a figure needs something the code cannot do, write the request for core into repro/scope/outbox_draft/ with the smallest option that would serve, and mark the row. (5) HANDOFF.md of the package for the next one (repro/figs): per figure the run ids, the files, the reader. README.md; JOURNAL.md.

items.title: reproduction of arXiv:2401.08530 section V: Langevin simulations

The authors' code is not public and their random realisations are their own: agreement is statistical, against the linear solution, and against the numbers the papers print. This track has already reproduced both scenarios of the first paper against the linear solution (ladder/, usr/, g2prod/, window/, a4res/, spec/scope/SCOPE.md, note/): build on that and do not redo it. PACKAGE repro/langevin: the numerical part of arXiv:2401.08530, section V (lines 782-882) with appendix D (noise amplitude) and appendix A (background): two coupled Langevin equations for the lapse and the e-folds of one patch in the uniform-field gauge. It is not a computation of numerical relativity; reproduce it with a reference integrator in Python in your package (numpy; registered runs through harness/bin/nrpic-run on processors, at most 6 cores). Prediction first for every figure and statement. (1) The background: plateau V = V_0 down to phi_c = 9.056, then V_0 [3 (phi/phi_c)^2 - 2 (phi/phi_c)^3]; phi* = 10, d phi/dN* = -2.0001, V_0 from the Friedmann constraint with H* = 1e-5, units M_Pl = 1; epsilon_1 and epsilon_2 against e-folds; check the paper's statements (ultra-slow roll from about two e-folds, the end of the plateau). (2) The pair of equations as printed (the equation for dN/dN_b and the one for d alpha/dN_b with its Ito term), the noise amplitude of appendix D evaluated on the background, the noise active between 2 and 6 e-folds, steps of 0.01 e-fold, fifty thousand paths, Stratonovich interpretation (the paper used the Stratonovich evolver of Mathematica: implement a Stratonovich scheme, Heun or stochastic midpoint, and cross-check with the equivalent Ito form). (3) The four figures remade in our style (harness/style: copy what you use into the package): a hundred paths of the lapse and e-fold differences to the background with their mean; skewness and excess kurtosis against time; the probability densities at N_b = 3, 4, 5, 6 with the Gaussian of the same first two moments and bootstrap confidence bands; the same in logarithm. Look at each figure and compare with the paper's (open the paper's PNG files from the store to look at them; never copy them). (4) The statements of the text, each tested by a run in which it could fail: exponential tails between 3 and 4 e-folds (fit); with the noise switched off at 6 e-folds the lapse returns to 1 and the e-folds are conserved; with alpha^3 set to 1 in front of the noise the densities become left-skewed; the Ito term changes the results little; and how much the results depend on the step (the paper says its tuning depends on the step of 0.01) and on the random seed. (5) Verdict per figure and per statement: REPRODUCED (how closely, by which measure), REPRODUCED IN PART, or NOT REPRODUCED, with what stays ambiguous in the paper (anything it does not state and you had to choose). results/*.json with every number; README.md; JOURNAL.md.

items.title: the equations of both papers checked and mapped to the source

The sources are read-only and never copied into git; their figures are never committed, and nothing read off a figure is committed as a data file (single comparison values with their locator may stand in text). The authors' code is not public and their random realisations are their own: agreement is statistical, against the linear solution, and against the numbers the papers print. This track has already reproduced both scenarios of the first paper against the linear solution (ladder/, usr/, g2prod/, window/, a4res/, spec/scope/SCOPE.md, note/): build on that and do not redo it. PACKAGE repro/equations: the equations of both papers, checked with computer algebra (sympy) and short numerical tests, by scripts in your package that a reader can rerun (registered runs on processors). Predictions first. (a) arXiv:2401.08530 sections II and III and the appendix of arXiv:2512.14649 'Gauge invariant perturbations as functionals of R': the scalar perturbations in each gauge as functionals of R, substituted into the linearised ADM equations and constraints. (b) The stochastic ADM equations (2401.08530 section IV; 2512.14649 sections 'Coarse-graining using R', 'Gauge invariant coarse-graining: field equation' and 'Full ADM Stochastic Inflation') and the BSSN form (2401.08530 appendix C; 2512.14649 appendix 'BSSN equations'): that the source terms follow from the window acting on the linear solution; that the coarse-grained constraints hold to first order in the noise with the sources as printed and fail at first order when one sign is flipped; the usual stochastic-inflation limit (2401.08530 section IV E). (c) The noise amplitude of 2401.08530 appendix D in slow roll and in ultra-slow roll against a numerical solution of the Mukhanov-Sasaki equation. (d) The Langevin pair of section V (the equations for dN/dN_b and d alpha/dN_b, with the Ito term) derived from the coarse-grained equations in the uniform-field gauge. (e) A table that maps every source term and every step of the stochastic scheme of 2512.14649 (its appendix 'Numerical and stochastic schemes' and the window) to the lines of athenak/src/scalar_field/ that implement it (read only; coord/INTERFACES/scalar_field.md, scalar_field_2.md, scalar_field_3.md), with the differences of convention (Z4c variables, the sign of K, units, the time variable). Per item: CONFIRMED, CONFIRMED WITH A CORRECTION (which: a misprint of a paper goes into ERRATA.md of your package as a [VERIFIED] row with its locator and the check that shows it), or NOT CONFIRMED (what fails, and whether the code follows the paper or the corrected form). EQUATIONS.md with the table; README.md; JOURNAL.md.
